articles.author: lakshay
articles.description:
Most productivity and habit apps today feel overwhelming—filled with noisy push notifications, gamified confetti, and expensive recurring subscriptions. 
I wanted something different: a calm, luxury monochrome discipline matrix inspired by the Stoic philosophy of daily self-mastery and the James Clear 1% compounding rule.
So I built and launched Chrono Matrix—a completely free, offline-first web application.
🔗 Live Web App: https://chrono-matrix-nine.vercel.app

💻 Open-Source Code: https://github.com/Lakshay-exec/chrono-matrix
Instead of just counting streaks, Chrono Matrix continuously calculates your momentum. Every completed ritual compounds your trajectory upward by +1%, while missed days model exponential decay over a continuous 30-day SVG vector.
The biggest problem with habit trackers is giving up after missing a day. Chrono Matrix features a 2-day breach protocol: if you abandon a habit for two consecutive days, an AI Disciplinary Council activates to assign fair, restitutive penalties to restore momentum.
Discipline requires biological energy. Chrono Matrix tracks nocturnal sleep consistency, midday power naps, and integrates with Google Fit movement telemetry.
Write a single definitive sentence about each day with instant mood labeling (▲ Ascending, ● Steady, ▼ Heavy). You can inspect any past date from the interactive ledger.
Your habits are personal. Chrono Matrix runs as an installable Progressive Web App (PWA) on desktop and mobile, persisting data locally with JSON export/restore.
Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, Vite
Animations: Custom magnetic fluid cursor, CSS micro-floats
AI Engine: Google Gemini API
Deployment: Vercel Global Edge Network
I would love to hear your feedback and suggestions! Try it out at https://chrono-matrix-nine.vercel.app.
articles.title: I Built Chrono Matrix: A Minimalist Habit Tracker with a 1% Compounding Trajectory

articles.author: CurlShot
articles.description:
If your service takes a URL from a user and renders it with Playwright, the obvious protection is to check the URL before page.goto(). I tested that on 2026-11-01 and it leaks. A public page that answers 302 Location: http://127.0.0.1/... made Chromium fetch the internal address, and the page content ended up in the rendered output.
Adding page.route() closes some holes and leaves the redirect one open. This post shows the three setups side by side, with the output, so you can see which request reaches the internal server in each.
Two local HTTP servers stand in for the real world:
internal on 127.0.0.1:4001 plays the cloud metadata endpoint or an admin panel. It records every path it receives.
public on port 4000 plays the attacker's page. Chromium reaches it as public.test through --host…
articles.title: Validating the URL before page.goto() is not enough: redirects slip past Playwright's page.route()

AI agents increasingly need to talk to other agents: hand off a task, pass a result, coordinate. Most of that traffic goes through someone's server in plain text. articles.author: StackVersus
articles.description:
OpenAI has updated its Help Center article on ChatGPT and Codex usage limits to say that, starting in December, the usage allowance on Plus, Pro and Business plans will be shared across ChatGPT and Codex. The change comes as OpenAI brings the agentic capabilities of Work into the main ChatGPT experience.
Usage for both products will be measured in tokens. How much of the allowance a task uses depends on the model chosen and the task itself, and more advanced models and complex tasks generally use more. Instant chat will not draw from the allowance. Combined remaining usage and reset times will appear in Settings > Usage.
OpenAI says it is preparing carefully to prevent disruption and expects most users won't need to wait for usage to reset more often than they do now. At the limit, users can wait for a reset, upgrade their plan, or buy credits to keep using eligible features.
The article does not give an exact December start date, token amounts per plan, or new five-hour or weekly figures. A separate OpenAI page on using Codex with a ChatGPT plan, updated about a week earlier, still says Pro plans currently have no five-hour limit and lists Plus local-message ranges per five hours. Those pages do not yet fully align with the shared model.
Developers and teams that split work between chat and Codex will draw from one pool, so a heavy coding session could leave less room for chat, and the reverse. Model choice also becomes a bigger cost lever, since advanced models consume more of the allowance per task.
Once the change takes effect, check Settings > Usage to see your combined remaining allowance and reset times. Confirm the December start date, per-plan token amounts and current five-hour limits on OpenAI's site before changing plans or budgets. If you rely on a heavier model, test your typical tasks now to estimate how quickly they draw down the shared pool.
Sources
OpenAI Help Center
Originally published on StackVersus, where prices and plan limits are checked against vendor pages and dated.
articles.title: ChatGPT and Codex will share one usage allowance from December

articles.author: Axonscape
articles.description:
An app built by Replit's Agent signs people in with their Replit accounts and keeps files in Replit's storage. Moved anywhere else, nobody can sign in. Change both first.
Deployed outside Replit, sign-in fails (REPLIT_DOMAINS isn't set), and saving or loading files errors.
server/replitAuth.ts signs people in through Replit's login service, and @replit/object-storage and @replit/database are Replit's own services. None of them exist outside Replit.
Ask Replit's Agent, or your AI tool, to switch sign-in to Clerk or Supabase Auth.
Move files to Cloudflare R2 or Supabase Storage, and Replit Database records into Postgres.
Bring the Postgres data along: in Replit's Shell, pg_dump -Fc --no-owner --no-privileges "$DATABASE_URL" > replit.dump.
Paste this into Lovable, Bolt, v0, Replit or Cursor:
This app has to run outside Replit. Replace sign-in with Replit accounts (server/replitAuth.ts, REPLIT_DOMAINS) with Clerk, and replace @replit/object-storage and @replit/database with S3-compatible storage (Cloudflare R2) and Postgres. Keep every page and API route working the same way.
The full page, with the request ready to copy, is at launchpad.axonscape.com/fix/replit-auth-outside-replit. I work on Launchpad by Axonscape, which runs a free launch check for apps built with AI tools: it finds this and the other things that break at launch, from a public GitHub repo or a .zip of the code, and keeps nothing.
articles.title: Replit Auth and Replit storage don't work outside Replit

Artificial Intelligence: Are We Teaching Machines to Learn or Just Recognize Patterns?


While exploring Machine Learning, I started questioning something fundamental:
Are we really teaching machines to learn, or are we mainly teaching them to recognize patterns from examples?
I believe there is an important distinction between learning individual examples and understanding the fundamental principles behind them.
An example is a specific situation from which we can learn something. A principle, however, is a fundamental truth, relationship, or structure that helps explain why something works.
These principles are particularly valuable because they can be reused across different contexts. Once we understand the underlying relationship, we can apply that knowledge to situations we have never…
